messages:
Raj: Heads-up — brought up hf->redwood conversion for the new 'orion-7b' fork and seeing surprising token-count + whitespace diffs. Repro below, can anyone else confirm?

Maya: pinging the tokenizer folks. quick paste of what I see. thanks for the repro, raj. :eyes: 

Raj: repro steps (local HF tokenizer vs converted rw tokenizer):
```
# HF (transformers) tokenize
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('orion-7b')
print(t.encode(' hello'))  # leading space
print(t.encode('hello'))
print(t.encode(' hello')) # non-breaking space

# Redwood converted tokenizer (rw_convert_hf) outputs different token ids / counts
# e.g. leading space preserved vs collapsed, and NBSP treated as normal space -> tokenization mismatch
```

Zack: can you paste the exact token ids? looking for byte-fallback differences (we had a bug where converted pretokenizer used byte-level fallback but also applied compatibility normalization).

Raj: sure — HF: [220, 1543, ...] for ' hello' (len 3). Redwood: [50256, 220, 1543, ...] (len 4) — extra pad/start token inserted because the converted pretokenizer is normalizing the leading space into a distinct byte-fallback sequence.

Maya: yikes. sounds like two separate issues: 1) unicode normalization mode changed (HF repo uses composed form for this model) and 2) our conversion pipeline enabled the ByteFallback pretokenizer in a slightly different order, causing a synthetic prefix token for leading whitespace.

Oliver: I ran a quick diff on config.json from HF vs converted: the HF tokenizer.json had "norm": { "name": "NFC" } and pre_tokenizer: null. Our converter set norm->"NFKC" and pre_tokenizer->{"type":"ByteFallback"} to match older models. That combo will change codepoint merging and then feed different bytes into BPE.

Raj: would that also change chat templates? We saw failing chat-parsing tests where messages starting with "\n" or leading space got extra tokens and tripped our chunking heuristics.

Maya: yes — chunking assumes token counts match HF. If leading spaces produce extra tokens we exceed per-turn budgets. Quick fixes: revert normalization to the HF-specified mode and don't add ByteFallback if HF tokenizer doesn't have it. Longer term: add a conversion validation step that compares token counts for a set of canonical strings (prefixes, NBSPs, combining marks).

Zack: I can push a tiny validator in rw_convert_hf that runs samples: ["hello", " hello", " hello", "é"] and compares lengths/ids. If mismatch, flag for manual review. Want to avoid silent diffs.

Raj: that would catch it. also — add a heuristic to keep HF pre_tokenizer exactly when present. our fallback to ByteFallback was well-intentioned for legacy models but is breaking parity.

ci-bot: ran unit tests on branch token-conversion-fix. 4 failing tests: token_count_parity, chat_chunking_leading_space, eval_script_integration, quantization-smoke. Logs: https://ci.redwood/integrations/1223

Oliver: quick workaround for product teams: in lowercase chat templates, we can trim leading spaces on the application side until conversion tool is fixed — not ideal but buys time. I'll start a doc with recommended mitigation.

Maya: agreed. I'll open a PR with: 1) preserve HF norm value, 2) do not inject ByteFallback when HF has none, 3) add the small sample validator. please review when ready.

Raj: thanks — flagging for release notes and a note for model-onboarding checklist ("verify tokenization parity on canonical prefixes") :white_check_mark: 

Zack: also let's add a quick fuzz-run for combining marks (e.g., e + COMBINING ACUTE) — we've had weird decomposed vs composed mismatches cause eval regressions.

Raj: good call. tagging this thread for postmortem if needed.

Oliver: thx all. I logged a short incident if anyone needs follow-ups: INC-2026-07-tokenizer-conversion (not a customer-facing outage, internal perf/regression).

Maya: will draft PR and tests today.

Raj: awesome — will try the branch later and report results. :rocket:
